We're working as partners, not as client and contractor. One rule before the task:

Not knowing something is not a failure. Saying "I couldn't verify this" or
"I don't have a real source for that" is a completely acceptable, useful answer
- it's information, not a dead end. The ONLY real failure is inventing something
(a source, a number, a quote, a repo, a bug) to make the answer sound more complete or
more impressive than it honestly is. You don't need to satisfy me with a
confident-sounding answer. You need to be honest with me about what you actually
know.

If you find something, cite it and quote what it actually says - don't
paraphrase a source into numbers it may not contain. If you don't find
something concrete, say so plainly and reason from what you do have instead.
An explicit "uncertain" section at the end is welcome and doesn't count against
the answer.

Research the officially documented context window and output token limits of the current Claude and GPT model families. Cite the vendors' own documentation pages and quote the limits.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Yes — I can keep this evidence-first format. I did not invent any model names or numbers beyond what is explicitly in the results I have.

What I could document is limited to the Claude family on Anthropic's official pages. The search results did not return a vendor-official GPT documentation page for context window or output token limits, so I am not going to guess those values.

### Claude / Anthropic

The clearest official context-window documentation I have says that several current Claude API models support 1M-token input windows, while some older ones remain at 200K, and that the API can emit up to 128K output tokens in a single request for the listed 1M-token models.

SOURCE: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows.md | QUOTE: "Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Mythos 5.1, Claude Fable 5, Claude Mythos 5, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Opus 5, Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Claude Mythos Preview have a 1M-token context window. A single request to any of them can generate up to 128k output tokens (`max_tokens`). Other Claude models, including Claude Sonnet 4.5, have a 200k-token context window." | CLAIM: These listed Claude API models have a 1M-token context window, can generate up to 128K output tokens per request, and at least Claude Sonnet 4.5 is documented at 200K tokens.

A separate official support article gives a simpler API summary and confirms the same broad split between 1M-token models and 200K+ models.

SOURCE: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8606395-how-large-is-the-claude-api-s-context-window | QUOTE: "The Claude API can ingest 1M tokens when using Claude Fable 5, Opus 5, Opus 4.8, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.6, Sonnet 5, or Sonnet 4.6, and 200K+ tokens (about 500 pages of text or more) when using all other models." | CLAIM: Anthropic's API context window is 1M tokens for the listed newer Claude models and 200K+ for other models.

There is also official support documentation for paid Claude plans, but it distinguishes product surfaces and model-specific caps. I am treating this as product-plan documentation rather than the raw API ceiling, because the numbers differ by surface.

SOURCE: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8606394-how-large-is-the-context-window-on-paid-claude-plans | QUOTE: "Claude Fable 5.1 1M tokens" | CLAIM: Claude Fable 5.1 has a 1M-token context window on paid Claude plans.

SOURCE: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8606394-how-large-is-the-context-window-on-paid-claude-plans | QUOTE: "Claude Opus 4.6 200K tokens" | CLAIM: Claude Opus 4.6 is listed at 200K tokens in the paid-plan surface documentation.

SOURCE: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8606394-how-large-is-the-context-window-on-paid-claude-plans | QUOTE: "Claude Sonnet 5 1M tokens" | CLAIM: Claude Sonnet 5 is listed at 1M tokens in the paid-plan surface documentation.

SOURCE: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-how-do-usage-and-length-limits-work | QUOTE: "On paid plans, the newest models support up to a 1M token context window, while others support 500K or 200K tokens. A portion of the context window is always reserved for Claude's response, so the longest possible conversation is slightly smaller than the full window." | CLAIM: Paid Claude plans include models with up to 1M-token context windows, with some at 500K or 200K, and part of the window is reserved for the response.

### GPT / OpenAI

I could not find an official OpenAI documentation page in the supplied search results that quotes current GPT model context window or output-token limits. Because you asked for vendor documentation only, I am not going to fill that gap from memory or secondary sources.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: official OpenAI vendor documentation for current GPT context window limits

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: official OpenAI vendor documentation for current GPT output token limits

### Uncertain

The only ambiguity here is that the support-plan page presents different context-window values depending on the product surface, while the API docs present the underlying model capabilities. I used the API documentation for model limits and treated the support pages as plan-specific product guidance.
